boundary: in-process shared service: per-request permission-profile resolution, authorization, execution and compact JSON serialization; excludes HTTP transport
build: cargo +1.88.0 test --release -p vulcan-app shared_query_stage_benchmark -- --ignored (VULCAN_MDB_PROFILE_SESSION=1, VULCAN_MDB_PROFILE_WATCH=1, VULCAN_MDB_PROFILE_READERS=8, VULCAN_MDB_PROFILE_SAMPLES=126, optional VULCAN_MDB_PROFILE_WRITES_PER_SECOND=2)
requests: eight reader threads sharing one watched session, each cycling the nine canonical fixture queries from a different offset; each reader's first request excluded; every request independently checked for exact totals, ordered paths, body omission, diagnostics and the 256 KiB bound
writes: optional writer thread applies body-only edits to one schema-valid contact record through plan_mdbase_write/apply_mdbase_write, paced to at most the target rate, then restores the record; the edits change no query result
host_conditions: shared development host with browser and agent sessions; load average about 9-11 during these runs; not the designated reference machine
findings: Readers no longer serialize: eight concurrent readers on one watched session measured p95 29 ms and p99 41 ms unrestricted without writes.

With the writer running, reader p95 was 36 ms and p99 49 ms, but writes took p50 1.9 s (first 18 s), so only 4 writes completed instead of 2 per second; the write budget, not reader concurrency, now blocks the mixed workload.

Managed writes refresh the vault note index but not the mdbase record cache, so after a write restricted readers fall back to source reconciliation until an unrestricted reader refreshes; a restricted 8-reader run was stopped after 10 minutes for this reason and is not reported.
